hook: Private employer workplace injuries dropped to 2.4 million in 2025.

sections.voiceover: Private employer workplace injuries dropped to 2.4 million in 2025.
b_roll: Graphic display showing a steep drop to 2.4 million workplace injury cases in 2025

sections.voiceover: On November 18, 2026, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics published federal workplace data. The annual tally fell 3% compared with 2024. Why did cases hit their lowest point since 2003?
b_roll: Document view of U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics report dated November 18, 2026
Bar chart comparing 2024 injury rates to 2025 showing a 3% decline
Timeline graphic sweeping back to 2003 marking historical low

sections.voiceover: But the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported 2025 marked the third consecutive annual decrease.
b_roll: Trend graph illustrating three consecutive years of declining injury counts

sections.voiceover: Federal records back to 2003 show 2025 reached an all-time low. Private employers reported 2.4 million total nonfatal injuries and illnesses. The 3% decline highlights three straight years of workplace safety gains.
b_roll: Historical line chart spanning 2003 to 2025 highlighting the historic low
Data graphic detailing 2.4 million nonfatal workplace injuries and illnesses
Progress bar chart showing 3% reduction over three consecutive years

sections.voiceover: Federal records logged 2.4 million nonfatal cases in 2025.
b_roll: Final summary card with federal data seal highlighting 2.4 million cases in 2025
